system.summary: One-part numerical French nomenclator, values 10-560, with homophonic letters, endings, syllables, words, names, places, and nulls.
system.notes: R852/R912/R922: key DECODE R639 headed De Monsieur de Bonac et Graffei; R852 uses an earlier issue of the table (same letters and syllables, different word codes). The Latin letter R483, once filed here, is in another key and is now rakoczi1711.

prior_solution.where: contemporary interlinear decipherments on the leaves (DECODE status Partially decrypted / Non-decrypted): R483 complete; R912 about 780 of 1,630 groups (page 1 except three lines, the first lines of pp. 2-3); R922 its first two lines (37 of 722); R852 a clear copy. About 820 of the 2,352 R912+R922 groups were deciphered at the time (extent recorded 30 Sept 2026).

conditions.human_role: Posed the target from the catalogue; supplied the DECODE session.

solution.what: Fetched the four DECODE text transcriptions (D2172, D2171, D2230, D1861).
Applied DECODE R639 (Bonac et Graffei key, already used for R902 in rakoczi1707) to R922.
Applied R639 to R852 and R912; both read as French reports to Rakoczi.
Applied R639 to the Latin R483: nonsense, so a different key.
Direction reversed for R852/R912/R922: Rakoczi is the recipient; R852 names Groffey in the third person.
Fetched all 14 page images and re-transcribed every cipher page (R922, R912, R852, R483) with image-reading subagents; about 40% of DECODE lines corrected, two dropped lines restored.
Read the R639 key image: 45=S and 47=T (DECODE 95/96), Z 54/55/110; the table skips 173/174, which the letters use as "de"; 561/562 = nt from context.
Corrected table on new transcriptions: R922 705/722, R912 1,586/1,630 groups keyed.
R852 found to carry its own clear copy (22 Jan 1706); its word codes differ from R639 (a different issue of the table).

Extent of the contemporary interlinear decipherment established from DECODE's transcriptions (PLAINTEXT lines: 29 on R912 p. 1, 5 on p. 2, 2 on p. 3; 2 on R922 p. 1) and the images: R912 about 780 of 1,630 groups (page 1 all but 54 groups), R922 37 of 722. About 820 of the 2,352 groups keyed with R639 were therefore deciphered at the time; the rest of R912 pp. 2-3, three lines of p. 1 and R922 after line 2 were read only here. The earlier write-up had mentioned an interlinear only for R483.

The three uninterlined lines of R912 p. 1 read with R639 after checking every group on the image and the key sheet: 'ni perdre de veue les affaires generales de l'Europe. Aussy publie-t-on comme une chose presque certaine qu'il n'entrera en Moschovie que la campagne qui vient'. Transcription corrected from the image (327? for 329 = pu, 87? for 57 = U, 589 for 509); M readings: veue (426 as ue), presque (343 as pres-), campagne (58 ns for 88 M), vient (534 Vienne + T). R912 keyed 1,585/1,630 (was 1,586).

Entry split under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the Latin letter R483, in Rakoczi's own syllabary with its interlinear decipherment, moved to rakoczi1711. This entry keeps R852, R912 and R922 in the R639 table; grades and fraction recomputed on R912+R922.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): tr/ image transcriptions; R912/R922 decrypts with the corrected R639 key; R852 its clear copy; key corrections copied from NOTES.md to texts/key.md

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): R912_image_read.txt and R922_image_read.txt read: syllable-split output with misreadings in most lines; no coherent sentences after the openings. Per-document D confirmed for both; relabelled decoded, not read; R852 reads from its clear copy; class read -> read in part; fraction_read 0.974 -> 0.182.

Re-read brief b22: every file on DECODE R912, R922 and R639 fetched with the project cookie (b17_fetch.py): one transcription each, the page images and the key image; no other attachment or comment. The R922 image shows a clear letter under the cipher sheet (fascicle p. 350, rotated, '... Altesse ... de Suede ...'), not imaged on its own: a possible clear copy, out of reach without an MNL image of pp. 348-350.

R912 p. 1 interlinear read on the image in eight native-resolution strips (texts/R912_interlinear_p1.txt) and checked group by group against tr/R912_p1.txt (b22_rk_lines.py); seven figure corrections seen on the image (416 -> 426, 473 -> 493, 147 -> 197 twice, 501 -> 301, 534 -> 504, 51 -> 81, 515 -> 315; texts/R912-R922_corrections.tsv). R922 ll. 3 and 17-18 checked on the image: figures as transcribed.

Readings texts/R922_reading.md and R912_reading.md: word division and normalisation by hand from the R639 decode, table words read for their sound, look-alike alternates where the groups give no French (R922 18 letters, R912 13 letters), holes marked; translations R922_en.md, R912_en.md. b17_score on the bodies: R922 0.839 (26/31), R912 0.783 (54/69); explicit holes 0.968, 0.899 (before: image reads 0.143, 0.25). R912 p. 2 keeps runs of holes; not re-read on the image (second pass not attempted). No key change adopted.

Consistency pass (cl): 'read in part' not justified because the second pass on R912 p. 2 is genuinely undone (not-attempted kept) and no print search is recorded (print step left unticked); NOTES already Status: in progress; outcome.gaps mirrors the list.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 3 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

Fuller reading of R912 pp. 2-3 from the figures of tr/R912_p2-p3 with the corrected R639 table (the DECODE page images need a login and were not re-read): fifteen holes worked (texts/R912_fills_2026-11-12.tsv, each row checked against tr/ and decode_tr.py). Read directly: 'les motifs de vostre commerce' (no group stood in the hole), 'parlé', 'en escrivant', 'l'a en mesme temps', 'du retour de vostre amitié', p. 3 'suit dans son procédé, tant [?à] l'égard de Vostre Altesse que de Monsieur le Palatin de Belz, son attachement pour les intérêts de l'Empereur' (over p. 3 ll. 1-2 the 1707 interlinear gives these groups mechanically, 'son propos' and 'ce de tant st le garde', and does not read 'procédé', which rests on the analogy of 344 propos for pro- with 343 present for pre-); 559 at the head of p. 2 l. 5 dropped as a line-opening filler. Five look-alike alternates, listed in texts/R912-R922_corrections.tsv: 177 -> 197 est, 195 -> 175 de, 328 -> 326 po (twice, 'points', 'qu'on n'estoit point'), 267 -> 265 lettre. The earlier unmarked j' for group 93 is now shown as [93]. read_share (v10 share) 0.946 -> 0.957 (803 -> 831 words, 46 -> 37 holes). One web search for a printed text (12 Nov 2026): none found.

Integration check (12 Nov 2026): the 15 rows of texts/R912_fills_2026-11-12.tsv re-checked with check_fills.py (all hold); read_share recomputed with the project formula (v10_relabel.share): 826 words, 42 holes, 0.952 as claimed, but four more unmarked places rest on sense alone (procédé, dire, ay, escrivant) and are now marked [?word] in the reading and the translation: 822 words, 46 holes, 0.947. R912 therefore stays read in part (state and read_share corrected); the read bar also needs no gap untried and the DECODE images of pp. 2-3 were not re-read.

Blind review of the 12 Nov reading by an independent AI language-model agent (grade B; the DECODE page images of pp. 2-3 need a login, so no sign was checked on the image): fills checked against tr/ and the R639 table, measures reproduced. Changes made after it: the five look-alike words marked [?est], [?de], [?points], [?point], [?lettre] in the reading and the translation; the procédé note corrected (the interlinear does not read it); the dropped group 129 (au) in 'Altesse, en escrivant' noted; the 'au premier ... au second' paragraphs joined. read_share 0.946 -> 0.952 (803 -> 826 words, 46 -> 42 holes). _check_reading on the whole file 0.707 -> 0.688 (the doubtful marks and the Notes section count); on the Reading section alone 0.500 -> 0.507. reading_review of R912 replaced (the 23 Oct review, grade B, described the earlier reading).

texts.label: R922, Dantzig, 28 Oct [1707]
texts.summary: A report to Rákóczi from Dantzig: a sale carried out for the Palatine of Belz (Elżbieta Sieniawska), with an authentic copy sent to the sieur Kray; orders for carbines; the writer is leaving to join the King of Poland and asks that Kray be given orders so he can continue his services at the Polish court. Deciphered with the corrected R639 key (unkeyed groups in [ ]).

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b22): the groups of tr/R922_p1-p2 (image transcription of 21 Sept) decoded with the corrected R639 table, divided into words and normalised by hand, the table words read for their sound (161 con, 395 son, 188 dont, 343 pre, 170 che ...); doubtful places checked on the image. 18 letters rest on a look-alike alternate (marque 244 -> 294, affaire 128 -> 123, estre 208 -> 207). Holes: groups 9, 873, 574, one '?' group and the run 'Ma D T hi'. b17_score on the body 0.839 (26/31), explicit holes 0.968; the image read 0.143.

texts.label: R912, 'au quartier', 5 Nov [1707]
texts.summary: A survey of Polish and Swedish politics for Rákóczi: King Stanisław, the Palatine of Belz and the Grand Hetman, the Muscovites, the King of Sweden's pacification and a new election, the Tsar, Rákóczi's letter to Rehnskiöld, Tököly; Charles XII will not enter Muscovy before the coming campaign. About half was deciphered between the lines at the time; the rest deciphered here with the corrected R639 key.

reading_review.note: Read at 0.952 by the contributor's count (0.947 on the strict count of 12 Nov 2026) with five look-alike words doubtful; pp. 2-3 not checked on the image (DECODE login). The new places of pp. 2-3 read as sense, the p. 3 passage on the court's conduct most strongly, and 17 of 18 sentences hold at no more than about one hole in ten words (the weak one is the passage on Tekeli).

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 94.6% of the words of texts/R912_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part. 12 Nov 2026: fuller reading of pp. 2-3 (texts/R912_fills_2026-11-12.tsv): 95.2% by the contributor's count (826 words, 42 holes). Integration check, 12 Nov 2026, strict count: four more places that rest on sense alone are marked [?word] and counted as holes (procédé, p. 3 l. 1, 344 propos read as pro- by analogy; dire, p. 2 l. 16, 276 -> 176 look-alike; ay, p. 2 l. 13, 533 -> 133 look-alike; escrivant, p. 2 l. 9, group 9 outside the table read as -nt and group 129 left out): 822 words, 46 holes, 94.7%. Under the 95% bar, so read in part; the DECODE images of pp. 2-3 were also never re-read (gap not-attempted).

texts.label: R852, Dantzig, 22 Jan 1706
texts.summary: The writer acknowledges Rákóczi's letter of 26 December, vouches for Groffey, and asks for a weekly Latin paper like the Mercurius hungaricus, since the German and Dutch gazetteers 'destroy the Kingdom of Hungary'. Its text is the letter's own contemporary clear copy (R852_clear.txt); R852 uses a variant issue of the table, so R852_key08_read.txt (R639 applied to DECODE's transcription) is a comparison only.
